title: Mid-Term Endorsements and Additional Premium — NFIP General Property Form and RCBAP Flood Policies (Write Your Own)
content:
**Kinds.** A mid-term endorsement on the NFIP General Property Form and RCBAP Flood Policies (Write Your Own) is recorded as one of: coverage increase, deductible decrease, mortgagee change, coverage decrease at renewal, or deductible increase at renewal.

**Status condition.** An endorsement is processed only on a policy whose status is pending effective or in force. The status is read from the policy record.

**Additional premium.** For a coverage increase or deductible decrease the rating engine returns the full-term risk premium and ICC premium for the policy as endorsed, and the additional premium is booked as endorsement components:
- the risk premium component is the increase in the full-term risk premium, multiplied by the days from the endorsement effective date to the term end divided by the days from the term start to the term end, rounded to the cent;
- the ICC premium component is the increase in the full-term ICC premium, prorated the same way and rounded to the cent;
- the Reserve Fund Assessment component is the tier's Reserve Fund Assessment percentage of those two pro rata amounts, rounded to the cent.

The endorsement effective date follows the waiting-period rule.

**Other kinds.** A mortgagee change takes effect on the date it is recorded and carries no premium. A coverage decrease at renewal or deductible increase at renewal takes effect on the next term start and changes premium only through the renewal booking; no mid-term credit is given for it.

## Status table

| Policy status | Endorsement processed |
|---|---|
| pending effective | yes |
| in force | yes |
| renewal grace, lapsed, cancelled or nullified | no |

## Worked endorsement (hypothetical figures)

Term of 365 days; endorsement effective with 146 days left; full-term risk premium rises from 4,000.00 to 4,500.00 and ICC premium from 70.00 to 80.00; Reserve Fund Assessment percentage 18.
- Risk premium component: 500.00 times 146 over 365, which is 200.00.
- ICC premium component: 10.00 times 146 over 365, which is 4.00.
- Reserve Fund Assessment component: 18 percent of 204.00, which is 36.72.
